column11: measured on Keytruda's own patients: drug_demand Keytruda, CMS Medicare Part B 2024, 107,476,784 dosage units over 75,361 beneficiaries = 1,426.16 mg a beneficiary. HCPCS J9271 is 'Inj pembrolizumab, 1 MG'. A full labelled year is 3,476.19 mg and it is the same number on either labelled schedule (200 mg every 3 weeks, 365/21 = 17.38 doses, or 400 mg every 6 weeks, 365/42 = 8.69 doses; the current KEYTRUDA label, DailyMed SPL setid 9333c79b-d487-4538-a9f0-71b91a02b287, version 228, effective 2026-07-10), so the schedule mix cannot move it. A beneficiary therefore averages 0.4103 of a labelled year on drug and 1 - 0.4103 = 0.5897 of the stock stops each year. The ratio is stable and drifting up across 2020 to 2024: 0.3787, 0.3930, 0.4060, 0.4057, 0.4103, so the stopping rate has fallen from 0.6213 to 0.5897 as the franchise moved into earlier lines and adjuvant settings
column12: measured on the same beneficiaries the price on file is quoted on, which is the whole point of the basis: the same CMS series gives $5,988,521,233 over 107,476,784 units = $55.71921 a mg allowed, so a full labelled year at the 2024 allowed rate is $193,691 and $79,464 / $193,691 = 0.4103, the same ratio. Pairing the labelled-year figure with this stopping rate would count the shortfall twice. For current scale rather than for the arithmetic: the CMS October 2026 Medicare Part B Payment Limit File (effective 2026-10-01 to 2026-12-31, on 2Q26 ASP data) sets J9271 at $62.253 a mg, so a labelled year now runs $216,403 at the payment limit and ASP itself is $58.729 a mg. Measured across every labelled indication rather than from one trial's median, which is right for an asset-level rate on a product sold in more than twenty tumour settings. Against it: dose holds, the 35-cycle label ceiling and weight-based paediatric dosing all lower mg a beneficiary and so overstate stopping
